claims.subject: graph factorization
claims.object: logarithm of the number of cooccurrences
claims.evidence_quote: For graph factorization, the weight between each pair of words is defined as the logarithm of the number of cooccurrences, which leads to better performance than the original value of cooccurrences.

claims.subject: DeepWalk
claims.evidence_quote: For DeepWalk, different cutoff thresholds are tried to convert the language network into a binary network, and the best performance is achieved when all the edges are kept in the network.

claims.subject: SkipGram
claims.evidence_quote: We also compare with the state-of-the-art word embedding model SkipGram [12], which learns the word embeddings directly from the original Wikipedia pages and is also implicitly a matrix factorization approach [8].

claims.subject: LINE
